clue.text: University engaged in supporting a quartet

indicators.note: something engaged in another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to be for something is to support it
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university student takes part in backing a string quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is a group whose membership totals the number that comes after three.

clue.text: Shifted one at 20 ft? Excellent

indicators.note: shifted letters are moved around out of their original order

blocks.note: the answer entered at 20-down
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether moving something to twenty feet would be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one at 20' points to the entry at 20-down, SATANIC, whose letters join FT in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is an informal word of high praise, a close synonym in everyday speech.

clue.text: Put out over work in the attic?

indicators.note: a word put out of place has its letters disturbed and rearranged

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
OP, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: A frustrated person put out by doing work in the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Up top is an informal phrase for the highest part of a house, where an attic would be found.

clue.text: A sample reduced vomit, but only just

indicators.note: a reduced word has been made shorter, losing its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a taste is a small sample of food
to retch is to heave as if vomiting

explanation.surface: A cut-down portion makes someone gag, though barely.
explanation.definitionFit: At a stretch describes something achieved with difficulty, by straining the limits, so barely managed.

clue.text: Overthrow overthrown, with involvement of daughter in royal house

indicators.note: something overthrown is turned upside down, which in a down entry means read from the bottom
involving something means taking it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a rout is a crushing defeat or overthrow
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty is toppled, a daughter being caught up in the coup.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English ruling dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Balanced analysis may form, finally, a standard of measurement

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the ends of three consecutive words
the metric system is a standard of measurement

explanation.surface: A careful analysis could eventually produce a fair yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something symmetric has matching halves, so its parts are evenly proportioned on either side.

clue.text: British author published a few

blocks.note: a newspaper that ran a story published it
some means a few

explanation.surface: A British writer has had only a handful of works printed.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote the children's sailing novel Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was an English writer best known for his children's adventure books set in the Lake District.

clue.text: Encourage sexual stimulation in gallery? It’s wrong internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so these words go within the gallery's name

blocks.note: the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain
the word it, the apostrophe-s being read as is
ill can mean wrong or harmful, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an erotic exhibit in a gallery is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is Britain's best-known group of art galleries, with its flagship sites in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to arouse interest, especially of a mildly erotic kind, which is a way of exciting someone.

clue.text: Beginning to dry after stockings covered in water?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
after places the dry letter behind the stockings word, though the clue mentions it first

blocks.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Stockings soaked through are starting to dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hosed is to be sprayed with a jet from a garden pipe, so drenched; the question mark flags this playful sense.

clue.text: Optimistic Bishop invested in universal fuel source

indicators.note: to be invested in something is to be clothed in it, so one piece is wrapped by the other

blocks.note: U is the film certificate meaning universal
B is the chess notation for bishop
peat is dug and burnt as fuel

explanation.surface: A hopeful bishop puts money into a fuel supply for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop's letter sits inside U followed by PEAT, after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat is an informal adjective for cheerful and positive in outlook.

clue.text: Continue to caress back, leading to a doctor’s initial set of comments?

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the preceding words are read right to left
initial means the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to pet is to stroke fondly
to go on is to continue
taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A doctor keeps stroking a patient's back, prompting a first round of remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the patient's body part, but it turns the preceding pair around; 'initial' reaches only the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a pad of paper on which remarks and jottings are written, so it holds a set of comments.

clue.text: Detailed section in record of meeting

blocks.note: a minute examination is a detailed one
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A detailed part is included in the record of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutes are the official written summary of what was discussed and decided at a formal gathering.

clue.text: Simple programme about energy plant

blocks.note: an applet is a small, simple software application
re means about or concerning
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A basic television programme about energy at a power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a power station beside 'energy', but here it means a growing thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple tree is a fruit-bearing tree, and every tree is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Drunk and frustrated after female’s left

indicators.note: something that has left has gone away, so that letter is no longer there

blocks.note: to be foiled is to be thwarted
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk and fed up once a woman walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' reads as time in the surface, but in the wordplay the thwarted word stands once the female letter has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is slang for intoxicated, much as well-lubricated describes someone who has had plenty to drink.

clue.text: What'll fill gap between 45 and 78?

blocks.note: surface reading: record speeds in rpm, suggesting some speed that sits between the single and the old shellac disc
setter's reading: the difference found by subtracting 45 from 78, itself the speed of an LP

explanation.surface: A record collector asks which disc speed lies between singles and old 78s.
explanation.walkthrough: 45, 78 and the answer are all record speeds, yet the answer is lower than both; it fills the gap arithmetically, as their difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy-eight minus forty-five gives this number, which is also the long-playing album speed.

clue.text: Unchanged in dialect after reinterpretation

indicators.note: a reinterpretation renders the material in a new form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: A phrase stays the same in a regional dialect after being reinterpreted.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer means unchanged while the letters have been completely changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical are exactly the same, with no alteration or difference between them.

clue.text: High-fliers not favouring white chess pieces?

blocks.note: first meaning: wealthy fashionable people who travel the world by air
second meaning: a player preferring the black set, jet being a glossy black stone

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is the black set of pieces, since jet means deep black; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The glamorous wealthy elite who fly between fashionable resorts are known collectively by this phrase.

clue.text: Help papers in getting behind article

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: Assistance with paperwork for someone who has fallen behind on an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting behind' puts the papers after the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is assistance or support given to someone in need, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Separate working gains edge

indicators.note: something being worked is kneaded and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: Splitting off a working operation gives a competitive advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To disengage is to detach or pull apart, as when gears are released from contact.

clue.text: Perhaps 8 ball initially dispatched - with this?

definitions.text: Perhaps 8 ball initially dispatched - with this?

blocks.note: surface reading: the black eight ball in pool being sunk
setter's reading: the clue asks for the instrument a player strikes with, the stick that sends any ball on its way

explanation.surface: A pool player wonders which tool will pot the black eight ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In pool and snooker the long tapered stick used to strike the ball carries this short name.

clue.text: Scents sheik dispersed, offering vague sensation

indicators.note: dispersed things are scattered about, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A sheik's perfumes drift through the air, leaving a faint impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchiness is a lack of detail or definition, the quality of an impression that is only roughly formed.

clue.text: Devilish selection of moves at an ice-rink

indicators.note: a selection is a run picked out of a larger whole, here consecutive letters from the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters spans four words

explanation.surface: A skater performs a wicked routine of jumps on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means relating to Satan, so fiendish or devilish in character.

clue.text: Harvest successful, though failing at outset

indicators.note: failing at the start means losing the opening letter

blocks.note: a winning side is a successful one

explanation.surface: A farmer's harvest turns out well despite a poor start.
explanation.definitionFit: Inning is an old word for gathering in crops, the bringing in of the harvest from the fields.

clue.text: Satisfied about Old Testament setting for church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a demand that is met is satisfied
OT is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone content with a church scene drawn from the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' suggests a place, but a musical setting is a composition of words to music.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, a musical setting of a religious text for church use.

clue.text: Biblical figure’s way of working: marine areas one cleared

indicators.note: cleared means emptied out, so that item is taken away

blocks.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working
seas are marine areas
a means one

explanation.surface: A biblical figure's method involved clearing a passage through the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the parting of the Red Sea; 's here is has.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses is the Old Testament prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the commandments.

clue.text: Editor, sound as a bell, not backing English scientist

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so that word is read right to left

blocks.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
ding is the sound a bell makes
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor in fine health refuses to support an English scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy, but it means a bell's noise. Arthur Eddington was an English astrophysicist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Eddington was a British astronomer who confirmed relativity by observing a solar eclipse.

clue.text: Biblical figure keen to follow God ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the closing letter of the word before

blocks.note: the closing letter
avid means eager

explanation.surface: A biblical character eager to follow God in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts the keen word after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: David is the shepherd boy of the Old Testament who killed Goliath and became king of Israel.

clue.text: American city beginning to turn Liberal in America

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the opening letter
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A US city starts to lean left politically.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in the state of Oklahoma, in the south-central United States.

clue.text: Supports a further course?

blocks.note: first meaning: backs a motion or proposal formally
second meaning: another helping of food after the first

explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests education, but it is a helping at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a motion is to back it, and having more of a dish is asking for another helping.

clue.text: Unoriginal article found in Roman dwelling

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a villa was a Roman country house
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a dull, unremarkable item in a Roman house.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla, by extension from the plain ice-cream flavour, means ordinary and lacking any special features.

clue.text: Considerate approach misinterpreted as idle coitus

indicators.note: misinterpreted things are read wrongly, so the letters come out in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone's thoughtful gesture is wrongly taken as a casual sexual advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care and concern for another person's welfare, a caring manner.

clue.text: Restrict attention from the press, declining deliveries

indicators.note: declining means refusing, so those letters are turned away and left out

blocks.note: press coverage is media attention
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

explanation.surface: Someone wants to limit media attention while turning down parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is six consecutive balls bowled by one player, so it is a group of deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To cage is to confine in an enclosure, so to restrict someone's freedom of movement.
